pm:coupling.pm:observed: across four quarters, each additional delivery engineer reduced out-of-hours escalations by roughly a fifth of a person on the rota; the two months the delivery teams ran two under establishment are the two months the rota overran. Neither member could observe this: neither files the rota.

pm:absent.pm:note: the rota is not metered against the delivery establishment, so nobody has sized how much of a person each engineer is worth

pm:coupling.pm:observed: the same planners schedule delivery work and the shift line. Across six quarters, the two quarters the delivery teams ran under establishment are the two quarters the line's schedule slipped, with no change to the line itself. Relieving delivery headcount visibly reduced the line's remainder, which is what the layers of a stack are assumed not to do.

asrt:fusion.asrt:observed: one delivery team under two employers. The queue is shared, work is assigned by skill rather than by entity, and either side has picked up the other's backlog within a week on eleven occasions this year. Fungibility is not total: language and the eight-hour offset make the Lisbon side unusable for US on-call, which is why `on-call` is a separate layer rather than part of this one.

asrt:elimination.asrt:observed: the US member commissions delivery work from the Portuguese member under an inter-company work order. Both file it as their own demand, correctly: the US member is asked for it and the Portuguese member does it. At group level it is one demand, counted twice. Sized from the work order's fee at the transfer rate.
payroll registers checked against each other for shared national identifiers; no person appears on both. The commissioned work moves hours, not headcount.

asrt:fusion.asrt:name: compute-us
asrt:fusion.asrt:observed: carried through unfused and renamed. It shares a token with the Portuguese member's `compute` and shares nothing else: a different vendor, a different contract, a different quantum, and a unit that does not convert to the other's without a utilisation figure neither member files. The rename is the composer's, and it is the fact that stops the two being silently added.

asrt:fusion.asrt:observed: one physical shift line, in Portugal, operated by the Portuguese member and scheduled onto by both. Fungibility is total and needs no argument: the parts are the same machine. The two parts cite different editions of the buffer vocabulary: the Portuguese part uses a translated edition, and the composed layer above cites the original. That choice is the composer's, and it is recorded here rather than left to look like agreement.
